KXMARMADHIGHSEED.note: No listing, title only. The outcome is the seed label of the deepest-advancing team, so it couples committee seed assignment with bracket advancement; futures_seed_other has both stages (committee S-curve plus 'advancement after seeding'). Low confidence kept; round and tie handling unverified.

KXMARMADREGION.note: Region winner is a single team surviving four bracket rounds; no seed variable enters the outcome. That is futures_champion's bracket-survival mechanism (its review covers title, finals and qualification on brackets), matching both earlier proposals and where KXMARMADROUND sits. futures_seed_other is centred on the committee model.

KXMARMADSEEDSUM.note: Title only, no listing. Sum of seeds (likely of Final Four teams) is a joint bracket outcome measured in committee seed units, which fits futures_seed_other's seed and advancement stages. A distinct seed-aggregate archetype is not justified: only 3 such series are in the pack and none has rules text.

KXMARMADSEEDWIN.note: Title only, no listing; most plausibly which seed line wins (the title or a round). It maps seed labels onto bracket results, so futures_seed_other fits, as both proposals said. The exact event (title vs game, which round) is unverified, so low confidence is correct.

KXNCAAMBACHAMP.note: Title 'College Baseball Championship' with no listing. Baseball is not men's college basketball, so OUT_OF_SCOPE:other_sport_college_baseball (declared, with a description) is right. Medium confidence is the cap without rules text, and the note about the possible ticker/title mismatch keeps the uncertainty honest.

KXNCAAMBAPANY.note: Rules: top 5 on the AP Top 25 in any 2026-27 poll, Preseason included. The outcome is AP voter output, which unreg:polls_and_awards' target names explicitly (poll rank). This is a named voted-ranking archetype, not a catch-all, so no new ap_poll_rankings archetype is needed. Quote verified verbatim.

KXNCAAMBAPCHURN.note: Rules count the distinct teams ranked #1 across all AP polls, Preseason through Final. 'Poll churn' / 'Teams to be ranked #1' is a listed contract type of unreg:polls_and_awards, so its process explicitly generates this outcome and a new archetype would duplicate it.

KXNCAAMBAPRANK.note: Rules: exact rank in the AP Final Rankings (expected Apr 6, 2027, after the tournament). The outcome is AP voters ranking teams, which polls_and_awards' poll-rank target covers. The final poll's dependence on tournament results is an input matter, not a separate archetype.

KXNCAAMBAWARD.note: Rules: the named player wins the stated award (here NCAA Tournament MOP), with a 1/N co-recipient payout and No if the player does not play. Voted individual awards are an explicit contract type of polls_and_awards. Only 2 award series are audited, under the >=4 split threshold, so no player_awards archetype.

KXNCAAMBCBC.note: College Basketball Crown winner, no listing. A multi-game postseason bracket winner fits futures_champion's bracket-survival mechanism (as the NIT does), not a single-game side market. Both proposals agree. Low confidence because settlement is unseen.

KXNCAAMBCONFAWARD.note: Rules: the named player wins a conference award (ACC DPOY), with a 1/N payout and No if the player does not play. The same voted-selection process as national awards, an explicit contract type of polls_and_awards. Quote verified. The award-specific criteria differ in inputs, not in archetype.

KXNCAAMBFIRST10.note: No listing for this ticker, but sibling KXNCAAMBRACE rules ('the first to score 10 points') show a team-level first-passage race. No existing archetype (final margin, totals, player points) produces a first-passage event, so the new race_to_n_points archetype (4 series) is legitimate. Low confidence is kept.

KXNCAAMBFIRST25.note: No listing; it is the 25-point version of the team race that KXNCAAMBRACE shows in rules text. A first-passage event belongs in unreg:race_to_n_points, not player_points. Whether a 25-point race can reach halftime or overtime is unverified, so low confidence is right.

KXNCAAMBFIRST50.note: No listing; it is the 50-point team race. At N=50 the event is close to the final-margin process but is still a first-passage event (a team can lead at 50 and lose), so unreg:race_to_n_points is right. Neither team reaching 50 is possible, and that settlement case is unverified.

KXNCAAMBHL.note: A conference tournament is a bracket-survival event. The CBB futures_champion review covers conference tournaments on a smaller bracket, and the identical KXNCAAMBHOR contract and about 30 sibling conference-tournament series sit in futures_champion. futures_conference's mechanism is season-long win totals and order statistics. Both proposals said futures_champion.

KXNCAAMBTOPAPRANK.note: Rules: the team is in the top 10 of the AP Final Rankings. This is the same voted-ranking mechanism as KXNCAAMBAPRANK with a bucket threshold, and it belongs in polls_and_awards' poll-rank target. Quote verified as a verbatim substring.

KXMARMADREGION.reason: 'March Madness Region Winner' has no listed markets. Yes most plausibly means the team wins its regional bracket (four games to the Final Four). That is single-team bracket survival, generated by futures_champion's bracket simulation, where Reach-Round series also sit. Settlement is unverified.

KXNCAAMBHL.reason: 'Horizon League conference tournament winner' has no listed markets. It duplicates KXNCAAMBHOR, whose rules read 'conference tournament champion' and which is ledgered under futures_champion with the other conference tournaments. A bracket-survival future, not season win totals. Settlement is unverified.
